::: {.callout-tip}
## Why This Matters
Incubated at IIT Delhi's FITT; promoter Prof. Abhisek Dixit (IIT Delhi, cryo-CMOS and qubit device researcher). Company says it signed a three-year service agreement (Apr 2025) to assess cryogenic aging reliability of GlobalFoundries' 22nm and 12nm CMOS, received DST-NIDHI seed approval (Sep 2025) and DLI design-infrastructure (EDA tools) support (Oct 2025). Current work is mainly characterisation and modelling; no tape-out publicly reported.
:::

## What does this firm design?

Cryogenic CMOS integrated circuits for quantum-computer control, space and defence applications.

**Why these scores**

- **Domain difficulty 5/5:** Domain difficulty 5: cryogenic (4K to mK) CMOS for qubit control; few firms worldwide.
- **IP ownership 3/5:** IP ownership 3: own cryo device models and PDK work; no chip architecture disclosed.
- **Design completeness 1/5:** Design completeness 1: no chip design or tape-out disclosed; activity is characterisation and modelling.
- **Market readiness 1/5:** Market readiness 1: no chip product; revenue appears to be characterisation services (GlobalFoundries SLA, self-reported).
